change: the TUI real-machine lane can run again, and it found two defects
why_it_could_not_run: tui-mount pinned @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui@0.11.1, which harness 0.2.0-rc.1 REFUSES on peer ranges. This repository already recorded the answer in docker/README.md — 0.11.2 is the first release whose ranges accept BOTH harness pins — and the Docker lane was moved at the time; the QA lane was not. The refusal then surfaced as the generic  SKIP, which reads as "not set up yet" about a setup that had just been attempted and rejected.
defects_fixed: the host pin: now 0.11.2, overridable with the SAME env knob the Docker lane uses (MPD_E2E_TUI_VERSION), so one variable moves both;
a refused host install is now its OWN prerequisite (), checked BEFORE , and it carries the harness's own rejection sentence;

the session reader looked for  while harness 0.2.0-rc.1 writes , so the preset witness could NEVER be found: measured, a real boot created a v4 store whose single decoded frame carries "agentPreset":"mpd" — the very value the lane reported missing. The reader now DISCOVERS the store version.

proves: profile bundles = [@deepseek-ai/dsh-base, @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui, @mpd-dsh/mpd] — the triple layer, in order
statusLine=true counters=true crashes=[] — the TUI booted on a real PTY through tmux and rendered, with ZERO apply-crash signatures
preset=mpd session=3cb80e26-618f-418c-9f6c-cb14e0e3a364 — the session really ran the mpd preset
rowComposed=true — the mpd-tui row is composed and names its dist entry point
isolationOffenders=0 — nothing landed outside the sandbox

tui_team_surface.one_cause: skills/dsh-qa/scripts/tui-team-surface.ts writeTeamFixture() writes the PRE-SPLIT layout , but the team-plane split (W1) moved the record to  plus the index . The scene therefore reads NO team and renders , which fails every downstream assertion (the phrase, the echo, the approval call, the outcome line) as a CASCADE from that one cause, not as ten independent defects.
tui_team_surface.why_this_is_the_lane_working: no unit arm could have caught this: the arms build their fixtures through the STORE, so they write the new layout by construction. Only a case that hand-writes a record on disk and then drives a REAL host can see the two disagree — which is exactly what this lane is for.
tui_team_surface.fix_needed: teach writeTeamFixture the post-split layout (the record body and the teams.json index), then re-run.

not_claimed: the team SURFACE itself is unproven on a real host until the fixture is updated; the failure is in the fixture, not evidence that the scene is broken
